subject: social
name: Social Studies
title: Grade 12 Social Studies: US Government & Economics
overview: Grade 12 Social Studies prepares young citizens for active democratic participation and global engagement through rigorous historical, political, geographic, and economic inquiry.
competencies: Evaluate complex primary sources, detecting bias, corroborating claims, and synthesizing context.
Analyze constitutional principles, governmental structures, and civil liberties in a democratic republic.
Apply macroeconomic principles, market mechanics, and fiscal/monetary policies to public issues.
Deliberate contemporary global policy dilemmas using evidence-based civic discourse.

modules.title: Foundations of American Democracy & the Constitutional Framework
modules.description: Analyzing separation of powers, federalism, the Bill of Rights, landmark Supreme Court cases, and civil liberties.

topics.title: Constitutional Architecture and Federalism
topics.description: Analyzing enumerated vs. reserved powers, judicial review (Marbury v. Madison), and checks and balances.

topics.title: Civil Liberties, Civil Rights and the Fourteenth Amendment
topics.description: Critiquing Supreme Court precedent on free speech, religious establishment, due process, and equal protection.

modules.title: Political Participation, Campaigns & the Three Branches
modules.description: Examining congressional lawmaking, the executive presidency, judicial appointments, elections, and special interest groups.

topics.title: Congress, the Presidency and the Federal Bureaucracy
topics.description: Tracing how a bill becomes law, executive orders, presidential war powers, and bureaucratic regulations.

topics.title: Elections, the Electoral College and Media Influence
topics.description: Evaluating campaign finance laws, primary voting systems, media bias, and voter turnout trends.

modules.title: Principles of Macroeconomics & Fiscal/Monetary Policy
modules.description: Investigating supply and demand, GDP, unemployment, inflation, the Federal Reserve Bank, and international trade.

topics.title: Market Mechanics: Supply, Demand and Price Equilibrium
topics.description: Graphing supply and demand curves, price elasticity, and analyzing market shortages and surpluses.

topics.title: Macroeconomic Health: GDP, Inflation and Unemployment
topics.description: Measuring real GDP, CPI inflation rates, structural/cyclical unemployment, and business cycles.

topics.title: Fiscal Policy vs. Federal Reserve Monetary Policy
topics.description: Analyzing government taxation and spending interventions alongside Federal Reserve interest rate decisions.
